text: Skip to main content Home › About › Strategic Plan Adopted Strategy · 2026–2030 Supporting the Champions of Regional Cooperation The Western Balkans Fund's second Strategic Plan, a refreshed, five-year roadmap that moves beyond grant-making alone to a more comprehensive, integrated and inclusive way of backing the people who make regional cooperation happen. Explore the Strategy View Programmes The Vision A region at peace with itself, integrated into its European home The Western Balkans Fund envisions a region where exchange and mutually beneficial cooperation between people, at all levels and from all walks of life, is the norm rather than the exception. Built with WBF leadership and the Secretariat, and shaped by the Council of Senior Officials of the six Contracting Parties, this plan is ambitious yet grounded, rolling out through a carefully phased programme of investment. Programme Mission “The WBF promotes ever closer cooperation and stronger ties between the Contracting Parties, their integration into the European Union, and a common presentation within and beyond the region, supporting the champions of regional cooperation through a diversified programme of grants, dialogue and technical assistance.” — WBF Strategic Plan 2026–2030 Theory of Change From direct support to lasting regional change By investing directly in regional initiatives and the champions who drive them, the Fund improves neighbourly relations that transcend geographical and cultural boundaries, and normalises cooperation as an essential part of a stable, prosperous, European future. 01 Invest Targeted grants & support to champions of cooperation 02 Connect Stronger, more resilient cross-border initiatives 03 Normalise Cooperation made visible & understood by the public 04 Reconcile Confidence, trust & cohesion across the region 05 Prosper Stability, development & EU integration for all Grant-making now sits within a stronger framework, reinforced by a convening role and by making information more accessible to the Fund's many stakeholders. text: Skip to main content Home › About About Western Balkans Fund The Fund Who we are The Western Balkans Fund (WBF) is an intergovernmental organisation based in Tirana, Albania, established by the governments of Albania, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Kosovo*, Montenegro, North Macedonia and Serbia. Conceived as a fully regionally owned and all-inclusive initiative, the Fund stands as a tangible expression of a renewed spirit of cooperation in the Western Balkans, a mechanism created by the region, for the region, to bring its people, institutions and communities closer together. WBF is the first home-grown regional mechanism that boosts cooperation through grants for civil society organisations and other stakeholders in the Western Balkans Six. Its founding reflects a shared conviction that lasting reconciliation and a common European future are built not only between governments, but between citizens, civil-society organisations and communities working side by side on concrete, cross-border projects. *This designation is without prejudice to positions on status and is in line with UNSCR 1244 and the ICJ Opinion on the Kosovo declaration of independence. title: Accessibility Statement
desc: The Western Balkans Fund’s commitment to an accessible website.
text: Skip to main content Home › Accessibility Statement Legal Accessibility Statement Our commitment to making this website usable by everyone. The Western Balkans Fund is committed to providing a website that is accessible, inclusive, and usable for everyone, regardless of ability, technology, or circumstance. We strive to design and maintain our website in accordance with internationally recognized web accessibility standards and continuously work to improve accessibility across all pages and digital services. Our accessibility efforts include: Clear and consistent navigation Readable typography and appropriate colour contrast Responsive layouts for different devices Keyboard-accessible navigation where possible Alternative text for meaningful images Structured headings and semantic HTML Continuous review of accessibility improvements Despite our efforts, some content or documents may not yet fully meet current accessibility standards. We are committed to addressing identified issues as resources permit. If you encounter accessibility barriers or require information in an alternative format, we encourage you to contact the Secretariat. We value your feedback and will make reasonable efforts to improve accessibility for all users.

title: Cookie Policy
desc: How the Western Balkans Fund website uses cookies.
text: Skip to main content Home › Cookie Policy Legal Cookie Policy What cookies this website uses and how you can control them. What Are Cookies? Cookies are small text files stored on your device when you visit a website. They help websites function correctly, remember user preferences, improve performance, and provide anonymous information about website usage. How We Use Cookies The Western Balkans Fund uses cookies to: Ensure the website functions properly Improve website performance and reliability Remember user preferences where applicable Analyze website traffic and visitor behaviour Enhance security and detect technical issues Where required by law, visitors will be asked to consent to the use of non-essential cookies. Types of Cookies Our website may use: Essential Cookies These are necessary for the operation and security of the website and cannot be disabled without affecting core functionality. Analytics Cookies These help us understand how visitors interact with the website so that we can improve content, navigation, and performance. Information collected is generally aggregated and does not directly identify individual users. Preference Cookies These remember user preferences, such as language or display settings, to provide a more personalized browsing experience. Managing Cookies Most web browsers allow users to manage or disable cookies through browser settings. Please note that disabling essential cookies may affect the functionality of certain parts of the website.

The Western Balkans Fund (WBF), established by the six WB Ministries of Foreign Affairs, has earmarked 15% of its core budget for gender equality initiatives . Through this mechanism, the Fund co-finances initiatives led by civil society organisations and other non-profit entities, helping them grow local project ideas into genuinely regional, cross-border collaborations. Apply here Meet past grantees PDF · 15 pages Guidelines for applicants Deadline 5 October 2026 12:59 CET Grant size EUR 500 – 3,000 up to 100% of eligible costs Implementation Dec 2026 – Apr 2027 final report by 30 April 2027 Applicant Type Individuals only one application per call About the Programme People-to-people links at the heart of regional cooperation MOVE Grants is a dedicated grant-making mechanism designed to support mobility, exchange, and people-to-people cooperation across the region. The scheme is built on WBF's belief that direct, in-person interactions whether through academic exchange, artistic collaboration, and/or professional mobility are vital to building trust, understanding, and shared values across the Western Balkans. Each MOVE grantee commits to an agreed structured mobility activity with a formal host institution/organisation in another Contracting Party of the Western Balkans Fund. After the visit, they share their experience within their networks, on social media and through WBF's platforms, becoming ambassadors for regional cooperation. The programme funds short-term, individual mobility within the WB6: Albania, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Kosovo*, Montenegro, North Macedonia and Serbia. text: Skip to main content Home › Our Programmes › Past Events Advocacy & Networking WBF Advocacy & Networking Events Building on its experience on regional cooperation and dialogue events, the Western Balkans Fund has become a recognized, visible and active promotor of civil society actors across the Western Balkans. Together with its longstanding partners, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Japan and the Embassy of Japan in Tirana, the Western Balkans Fund hosts events addressing critical issues related to regional cooperation, dialogue, and reconciliation. These themed and WBF-facilitated events involve relevant stakeholders not only from the region and European Union, but also from all over the world. 2026 #LeadBalkans 2025 SYNERGY 2023 VerityCon23 2023 UNSTOPPABLE 2022 FIRE 2020 CSO Summit Western Balkans Diaspora #LeadBalkans Conference February 2026 Tirana, Albania Held in Tirana in February 2026, the #LeadBalkans Conference was a flagship regional event dedicated to strengthening cooperation between the Western Balkans and its diaspora communities. 3 days 6 panels 100 diaspora and community leaders participated The conference was built around a clear premise: while regional cooperation in the Western Balkans is becoming stronger and more structured, diaspora communities are still frequently left outside these processes . Therefore, their knowledge, professional experience, international connections and capacity to contribute to the region’s development remain insufficiently integrated into regional initiatives and policymaking. To address this gap, the Western Balkans Fund brought together more than 100 diaspora representatives from across the Western Balkans. Participants travelled to Tirana from over 20 countries, stretching from the United States to Japan , reflecting the extraordinary geographical reach and diversity of the region’s diaspora. Diaspora is the best ambassador of our culture and a crucial partner in supporting development and strengthening vital connections between our region and the wider world. title: Peer to Peer
desc: Peer to Peer is a capacity-building programme strengthening Western Balkans civil society through expert-led learning, peer exchange and EU partnerships.
heads: A Journey of Learning and Collaboration
Connecting the Western Balkans with Europe
Building Stronger Civil Society Across the Region
text: Skip to main content Home › Peer to Peer Flagship Capacity-Building Programme Strengthening Civil Society through Regional Learning and European Partnerships Peer to Peer connects civil society organisations across the Western Balkans with their counterparts in the European Union. Implemented by the Western Balkans Fund and funded by Germany's Federal Foreign Office, the programme brings together 12 organisations from all six Contracting Parties for a full cycle of exchange and capacity building: expert-led training in monitoring and evaluation, strategic communication and countering misinformation, followed by mentoring, study visits with EU peer organisations and local trainings that pass the knowledge on across the region. Why Peer to Peer Why the Programme Matters Civil society organisations across the Western Balkans operate in an increasingly complex environment shaped by evolving funding landscapes, growing public expectations and rapidly changing information ecosystems. Building resilient organisations today requires more than technical expertise. It requires strong governance, effective communication, evidence-based decision making and the ability to respond to misinformation while maintaining public trust. Peer to Peer gives participating organisations the space to address these challenges together, connecting with peers, field experts and counterparts in the European Union, and taking the time to reflect, reshape and reimpact. Add image why-peer-to-peer.jpg One programme, four connected formats A Journey of Learning and Collaboration The Peer to Peer journey combines intensive expert training, one-to-one mentoring and first-hand exchange with European civil society organisations. Introduction The Western Balkans Fund ("WBF", "the Fund", "we", "our", or "us") respects your privacy and is committed to protecting the personal information you provide when using our website, online application platform, and related digital services. We process personal data responsibly, fairly, and transparently, in accordance with applicable data protection laws and internationally recognized privacy principles. This Privacy Policy explains what information we collect, why we collect it, how it is used, how it is protected, and the rights available to individuals whose personal data we process. Who We Are The Western Balkans Fund is an international organization established by the Governments of Albania, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Kosovo*, Montenegro, North Macedonia, and Serbia to promote regional cooperation, good neighbourly relations, and sustainable development throughout the Western Balkans. *This designation is without prejudice to positions on status and is in line with UNSCR 1244 and the ICJ Opinion on the Kosovo declaration of independence. The WBF Secretariat, based in Tirana, Albania, acts as the controller of personal data collected through this website. For privacy-related enquiries, please contact: Email: info@westernbalkansfund.org Information We Collect Depending on your interaction with the Fund, we may collect: Name and surname Organization or institution Professional title Email address Telephone number Country of residence Information submitted through contact forms Grant application and project documentation Event registration details Newsletter subscription information Technical information such as IP address, browser type, operating system, device information, pages visited, and website usage statistics We collect only the information necessary to provide our services and fulfill our institutional responsibilities. title: Regional Dialogue Sessions
desc: Western Balkans Fund events centred on dialogue and people to people links, bringing grantees, applicants, donors, policymakers and experts together around regional cooperation.
heads: RNDS on Education and Scientific Exchange (Skopje, 7-8 November 2024)
text: Skip to main content Home › Our Programmes › Regional Dialogue Sessions Advocacy & Networking Regional Dialogue Sessions WBF actively organizes events that centre around dialogue and people to people links. These events serve as platforms for stakeholders to participate in constructive dialogues and strengthen people to people links. The primary objective of these activities is to emphasize the significance of regional cooperation. During these events, stakeholders have the opportunity to express their perspectives, share insights, and discuss pertinent issues among each other and continue fostering a collaborative and open dialogue that not only highlights the importance of regional cooperation but also facilitates a meaningful exchange of ideas and viewpoints. These events play a crucial role in promoting understanding, cooperation, and networking efforts in support of regional development goals within the Western Balkans. WBF takes a proactive approach, involving a broad spectrum of stakeholders, including its grantees, potential applicants, donors, policymakers, and experts. These inclusive dialogues platforms aim to provide a comprehensive understanding of the challenges and opportunities surrounding regional cooperation. Networking opportunities embedded in these events facilitate relationship-building among participants, laying the groundwork for sustained collaborative efforts. How It Works How the dialogue unfolds 1 Bringing stakeholders together WBF takes a proactive approach, convening a broad spectrum of stakeholders around dialogue and people to people links. 2 Perspectives and insights Participants express their perspectives and share insights, discussing pertinent issues among each other. 3 An exchange of ideas Open discussion builds a comprehensive understanding of the challenges and opportunities surrounding regional cooperation. 4 Relationships that continue Networking built into each event turns that exchange into relationships, and the groundwork for sustained collaborative efforts. desc: WB6-V4 Fellowships fund short-term academic stays for PhD students and doctoral holders between the WB6 and the V4 — 2–10 weeks, €500/week.
heads: Academic mobility that connects two regions
text: Skip to main content Home › Our Programmes › WB6-V4 Fellowship A joint programme of WBF & the International Visegrad Fund Currently Closed — Next call opens April 2027 WB6-V4 Fellowship Short-term academic fellowships for PhD students and doctoral holders, moving in both directions between the Western Balkans (WB6) and the Visegrad Group (V4). Conduct research, lecture, or study in archives and libraries across the two regions. Jointly funded by the Western Balkans Fund and the International Visegrad Fund. Applications are submitted through the My Visegrad portal . Eligibility for next call Programme page on IVF Scholarship €500 / week Duration 2 – 10 weeks Travel grant Up to €500 Who can apply PhD students & holders Direction WB6 ↔ V4 Who can apply Eligibility Full-time doctoral students or holders of a doctoral degree Citizens of the WB6 applying to host institutions in the V4 Citizens of the V4 applying to host institutions in the WB6 Open to the targeted audience regardless of current affiliation Host must be relevant to the fellowship's nature Full conditions What you receive Funding €500 per week lump-sum scholarship Paid in two instalments — ~80% on arrival, remainder on report Optional travel grant up to €500 based on estimated costs Duration: 2 to 10 weeks Funding details 2026 Call · Completed Results announced 13 Apr 2026 Call opened 17 May 2026 Applications closed June 2026 51 fellowships approved About the Programme Academic mobility that connects two regions The WB6-V4 Fellowships allow WB6 citizens to apply for short-term fellowships at V4 research institutions (in Czechia, Poland, Hungary, or Slovakia). Reciprocally, V4 applicants can apply for fellowships at WB6 institutions (in Albania, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Kosovo* or Serbia). The programme is jointly funded by the International Visegrad Fund and the Western Balkans Fund , reflecting a shared commitment to academic cooperation and people-to-people links between the two regions.
